claims.text: The initial Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy is a single-phase BCC alloy.
Asymmetric XRD peaks in the initial alloy arise from dendritic–interdendritic compositional micro-segregation.
The Cr-free baseline has low room-temperature fracture strain because of micro-segregation and the absence of secondary-phase reinforcement.
Adding approximately 4 at.% Cr will induce a multicomponent C15 or C14 Laves phase.
The Cr-induced Laves phase will have a volume fraction of approximately 4%.
Cr will preferentially partition into interdendritic regions of the as-cast alloy.
Cr partitioning will produce a reticulated, interconnected Laves-phase network along interdendritic boundaries.
The reticulated Laves network will impede crack extension by deflecting cracks along phase boundaries and increasing fracture-surface area.
Cracks crossing the network will require additional energy to fracture the brittle Laves phase.
The reticulated Laves phase will provide crack bridging.
Atomic-size mismatch and electronegativity differences associated with Cr will distort the BCC matrix lattice.
Cr-induced lattice distortion will increase Peierls or friction stress for dislocation motion and produce solid-solution hardening.
Solid-solution hardening will raise yield strength and may delay necking.
The Cr-added BCC matrix will contract by more than approximately 0.02 Å relative to the Cr-free alloy.
The magnitude of BCC lattice contraction will correlate with the Laves-phase volume fraction.
A BCC lattice-parameter contraction indicates successful Cr incorporation and phase stability.
The Cr-added alloy will have higher room-temperature fracture strain than the Cr-free baseline.
The Cr-added alloy will remain less ductile than theoretical single-phase expectations because Laves phases are brittle.
Observing a reticulated Laves phase only in the Cr-added alloy, despite comparable segregation patterns and thermal histories, would distinguish Cr-specific phase formation from segregation alone.
The proposed morphology-based mechanism requires a reticulated phase fraction between approximately 1 and 10 vol.%, rather than isolated particles or a fraction outside that range.
